subject: general
question: When does a vacuum booster create a vacuum?

options.text: When the engine is off, and brake is applied
When the engine is running, and the brake is not applied
When the fuel level is low

solution:
The correct answer is __When the engine is running, and the brake is not applied**(Option 2)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Vacuum booster__ is a component of the braking system that amplifies the force applied to the brake pedal.
 
• A vacuum is created when the engine is running, which is essential for the booster to function effectively.
 
• When the brake is not applied, the vacuum booster is in a ready state to assist braking.
 
• The vacuum is generated either from the intake manifold of the engine or by a dedicated vacuum pump in some vehicles.
 
• This ensures smooth and effective braking by reducing the effort needed by the driver.
 
• When the engine is off, the vacuum booster cannot generate a vacuum, making braking harder.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Brake Booster Types:**

 
 
• Single diaphragm boosters are used in smaller vehicles.
 
• Dual diaphragm boosters are used in larger vehicles for more braking power.
 
 
 
• **Electric Vacuum Pumps:**
 
 
• Modern vehicles, especially electric and hybrid, use electric vacuum pumps for braking.
 
• These pumps ensure consistent vacuum creation even when the engine is not running.
